subject: Post-call: Dedicated GPU residency, isolation & scaling — proposed SLA targets
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Bhandari <maya@orion-robotics.com>, Ruben Ortiz <ruben.ortiz@orion-robotics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Dedicated GPU residency, isolation & scaling — proposed SLA targets

Hi Maya / Ruben —

Thanks again for the call earlier. I wanted to capture the key points and proposed next steps so nothing falls through the cracks. TL;DR: Orion is leaning toward a small dedicated pool with strict tenant isolation and a burstable scale policy; initial SLA ask is 99.9% uptime and sub-200ms median token latency for your inference endpoints.

Recap of pain / goals (what you told us):
- Performance variability on shared endpoints is blocking field demos and slow model iteration (latency spikes during peak testing windows).
- Data isolation: legal requires a dedicated environment for customer models and audit logs retained for 13 months.
- Predictable cost: finance wants committed spend (monthly) rather than pay-as-you-go surprises.

Proposed dedicated capacity profile (what we recommend):
- Pool: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) with tenant isolation (dedicated VGPU assignment + network segmentation).
- Burst: auto-burst up to +4 GPUs for short peak windows (policy-based, 15-minute cool-down).
- Autoscale triggers: queue depth + 95th latency per model; manual guardrails for cost control.

SLA targets and observability:
- Target SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime for endpoint availability.
- Latency objectives: 95th percentile <350ms; median token latency target <200ms for your 512-token prompts.
- Logging / audit: per-request audit logs, 13-month retention, KMS-integrated key control for model artifacts.

Open items / risks we discussed:
1) Model sizes & KV cache behavior — if you move to longer context lengths we’ll need a separate perf pass; this could change GPU count.
2) Procurement timeline — PO + security questionnaire turnaround will drive start date.
3) Network isolation for on-site CI systems — may need our Private deployment checklist if you want the control plane isolated.

Attachments: I attached a short SLA draft and the workload profiling sheet we discussed. Please review the SLA section (page 2) where I called out uptime/latency targets and escalation contacts.

Suggested next steps (ordered):
1) You review the attached SLA draft and workload profile — flag questions by Fri 2026-06-12.
2) We run a quick perf / sizing validation with a synthetic workload (30–60 minute run) once you approve the profile.
3) If sizing looks good, Marissa will prepare a one-page commitment + pricing and we’ll route through procurement.

Can you confirm timeline expectations for procurement and whether legal will need any additional contract language for data residency?

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0134
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sla_draft_v1.pdf (10 pages), orion_prod_workload_profile.xlsx (workload snapshot)

From: Maya Bhandari <maya@orion-robotics.com>

Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated GPU residency, isolation & scaling — proposed SLA targets

Thanks Vivek — solid write-up, much appreciated. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 8x A100 equiv seems reasonable as a starting point. We plan to run larger model variants next quarter (context up to 8k) — can you call out the perf-pass assumptions that could change counts?
- Procurement: finance expects to sign a monthly reserved contract but we need a short SOW + pricing to present to the budget committee by 2026-06-24.
- Legal: data residency is non-negotiable; the 13-month audit log retention is fine but please add language around export controls and vendor access (we can share a redline).

Ruben also confirmed we can do the perf validation next Tue 2026-06-16 morning (PDT). Can you confirm availability and what telemetry we’ll need from our side?

Also: attaching our product team’s rough model distribution so you can see the expected memory footprint per model.

Maya
CTO — Orion Robotics
maya@orion-robotics.com | +1 617-555-2290

I’ll draft the one-page commitment + preliminary pricing today. Aisha — please prep the perf-run checklist (telemetry to collect: p95 latency, median token latency, GPU memory utilization, KV cache hit rate, tail queue depth).

Vivek — can you schedule the 30–60m perf window with Maya and Ruben and include the test harness repo link? I’ll start the pricing doc and attach the SLA draft.
